jobs.title: AVP, Enterprise Digital Capabilities
jobs.description:
We are seeking a strategic, collaborative and product-minded leader to join our team as Assistant Vice President (AVP), Enterprise Digital Capabilities. This role is a key leader in Manulife's multi-year transformation to modernize and converge our digital ecosystem across Canada, the US, Asia and Global Wealth & Asset Management.

At the heart of this role is a simple objective: identify what is common across our digital experiences, build it once as an enterprise capability, and enable markets and segments to reuse and extend it to accelerate their own digital roadmaps.

Manulife has established a strong portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities that support our Digital Storefront transformation and broader unification ambitions. The next opportunity is to expand and scale this portfolio to accelerate the unification strategies and roadmaps of our segments and advance One Manulife experiences across the enterprise. The AVP will lead this evolution – working across segments to identify where common capabilities can create the greatest incremental value, bringing together requirements to ensure capabilities are designed for enterprise reuse, defining adoption and rollout strategies, and establishing a federated model where capabilities can be developed globally or contributed by segments and scaled for broader enterprise benefit.

The AVP will own the strategy and evolution of this portfolio — identifying new opportunities for reuse, prioritizing investment, establishing strong product management disciplines, driving adoption, optimizing existing capabilities and ensuring that each enterprise investment continues to deliver measurable value.

A critical part of the role is leading the Common Capability Collective, bringing together digital and product leaders from across the enterprise to identify common needs, align roadmaps, determine where enterprise investment can eliminate duplication and accelerate delivery, and create a shared view of capability priorities.

This is an enablement role, not ownership of individual market or segment experiences. The AVP will partner closely with Digital Storefront and segment digital leaders to understand their roadmaps and determine how enterprise capabilities can help them deliver faster, with greater quality, consistency and efficiency.

The AVP will operate in a two-in-a-box partnership with a complementary Global Technology leader, jointly shaping the business and technology evolution of enterprise digital capabilities. Together, they will ensure capabilities are scalable, secure, reusable, well-integrated and designed for long-term enterprise value.

Position Responsibilities

Enterprise Capability Strategy & Portfolio

Own the strategy, roadmap and ongoing evolution of Manulife's portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities.
Establish a clear view of the capabilities required to support digital convergence across markets, segments and channels.
Continuously identify common business and customer needs that can be solved once and reused across the enterprise.
Assess existing segment capabilities for opportunities to scale them globally rather than rebuilding equivalent solutions.
Prioritize enterprise investment based on customer value, segment demand, reuse potential, strategic alignment and economic benefit.
Maintain a multi-year capability roadmap aligned to Digital Storefront, segment roadmaps and Manulife's broader digital strategy.
Ensure the portfolio remains focused and sustainable by rationalizing overlapping capabilities, technology and licenses where appropriate.

Common Capability Collective & Federated Leadership

Lead the Common Capability Collective, bringing together Digital Storefront and product leaders from across the enterprise to jointly shape capability priorities and investment.
Create transparency across segment roadmaps to identify shared needs, opportunities for reuse and potential duplication before investment occurs.
Establish a federated model that enables capabilities to originate within segments where appropriate and subsequently evolve into reusable enterprise capabilities.
Build alignment around enterprise standards and shared capabilities while preserving segment accountability for their own customer experiences and business outcomes.
Create clear decision rights, funding principles, ownership models and governance for the creation and evolution of common capabilities.

Product Management & Capability Evolution

Establish strong product management disciplines across the enterprise capability portfolio, including product vision, roadmaps, adoption, performance measurement and lifecycle management.
Ensure every capability has clear customer and business outcomes, ownership, success measures and an evolution roadmap.
Use segment feedback, performance data and emerging customer needs to continuously improve capabilities.
Drive adoption and reuse across markets and segments, ensuring enterprise investments translate into meaningful acceleration of local roadmaps.
Ensure capabilities are designed for extensibility so segments can meet differentiated market needs without unnecessarily duplicating core functionality.
Manage capabilities through their full lifecycle, including investment, enhancement, optimization, consolidation and retirement.

AI Enablement & Optimization

Establish an AI-by-default approach to the development and evolution of enterprise digital capabilities.
Identify opportunities to embed AI directly into capabilities to improve customer experiences, decisioning, personalization and digital effectiveness.
Apply AI and automation across the capability lifecycle to accelerate development, testing, implementation, operations and ongoing optimization.
Partner with Technology and enterprise AI teams to identify emerging AI capabilities that can be productized and reused across the organization.
Continuously evaluate opportunities to reduce manual effort, improve quality and accelerate time to market through AI-enabled capabilities and ways of working.

Enterprise Integration & Technology Partnership

Co-lead the enterprise capability portfolio in close partnership with Global Technology through a two-in-a-box leadership model.
Define business requirements and product priorities while partnering with Technology on architecture, engineering, security, scalability and technical lifecycle management.
Ensure enterprise capabilities are designed to integrate effectively across Manulife's digital ecosystem and can be consumed by multiple platforms, markets and channels.
Promote API-enabled, modular and reusable approaches that reduce point-to-point solutions and technology duplication.
Ensure platform and technology decisions support long-term reuse, interoperability and enterprise scale.

Business Value & Benefits Realization

Establish a clear value proposition and business case for enterprise digital capabilities and the overall portfolio.
Quantify and track the value generated through reuse, including delivery acceleration, avoided duplicate investment, license consolidation, operational efficiency, improved customer experience and reduced ongoing support costs.
Demonstrate how building once and reusing at scale compounds speed, quality and efficiency with every additional implementation.
Partner with Global Marketing Strategy, FP&A, Technology and segment teams to track expected and realized benefits.
Use adoption, utilization, performance and financial data to inform ongoing investment and portfolio decisions.

Adoption & Enterprise Enablement

Partner with segment digital leaders to understand upcoming priorities and proactively identify enterprise capabilities that can accelerate their roadmaps.
Establish clear onboarding, documentation, implementation patterns and support models that make enterprise capabilities easy for teams to adopt.
Build awareness and understanding of available capabilities across the organization to increase reuse and prevent unnecessary reinvention.
Create feedback loops with consuming teams so capabilities continue to evolve based on real implementation and customer needs.
Champion a culture of reuse and enterprise thinking while recognizing the differentiated needs of individual markets and businesses.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Business, Digital, Technology, Marketing or a related discipline; MBA or master's degree preferred.
10+ years of experience in digital product management, digital transformation, enterprise capabilities, platforms or related leadership roles.
Demonstrated experience building and scaling reusable digital products, platforms or capabilities across a complex, federated organization.
Strong understanding of modern digital ecosystems, including APIs, cloud platforms, identity, personalization, search, content, data, analytics, experimentation and customer experience technologies.
Experience establishing product management disciplines and managing a portfolio of digital products or capabilities through their lifecycle.
Demonstrated ability to identify opportunities for reuse, simplify complex technology landscapes and translate enterprise investment into measurable business value.
Strong understanding of AI and automation and their application to digital products, customer experiences and delivery.
Proven ability to influence and align senior stakeholders across business, marketing, product and technology organizations without relying solely on direct authority.
Experience operating successfully in a global, federated environment with competing priorities and varying levels of digital maturity.
Strong strategic, commercial and analytical skills, with the ability to connect technology and capability decisions to customer outcomes, delivery acceleration and financial value.
Exceptional communication and leadership skills with the ability to translate complex digital concepts into clear business outcomes.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means Manulife increasingly builds once and benefits many times.

Segments are able to deliver their digital roadmaps faster because proven enterprise capabilities are readily available rather than repeatedly designed, procured and built. Capabilities originating in one part of Manulife can be scaled for the benefit of others. Duplicate technology and investment decline. Adoption and reuse increase. AI and automation continuously improve how capabilities are built, operated and consumed.

Over time, Manulife develops a growing portfolio of reusable digital capabilities that compounds the value of each investment — accelerating delivery, improving quality and customer experience, reducing duplication and creating sustainable enterprise-scale benefits.

When You Join Our Team

As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.
We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.

The role being advertised is an existing vacancy.

About Manulife And John Hancock

Manulife Financial Corporation is a leading international financial services provider, helping people make their decisions easier and lives better. To learn more about us, visit https://www.manulife.com/en/about/our-story.html.

Manulife is an Equal Opportunity Employer

At Manulife/John Hancock, we embrace our diversity. We strive to attract, develop and retain a workforce that is as diverse as the customers we serve and to foster an inclusive work environment that embraces the strength of cultures and individuals. We are committed to fair recruitment, retention, advancement and compensation, and we administer all of our practices and programs without discrimination on the basis of race, ancestry, place of origin, colour, ethnic origin, citizenship, religion or religious beliefs, creed, sex (including pregnancy and pregnancy-related conditions), sex

jobs.title: DIRECTOR OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Business travel expense account for trips outside your usual work area

Join a growing network and become a key player in the future of private medicine in Quebec.

Apply now and make a real difference.

jobs.title: AI Learning Associate Director - Learning and Development (18-month contract)
jobs.description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

AI is transforming how organizations operate, create value, and develop talent. As EY Canada accelerates its AI transformation, L&D continuous to play a critical role in helping our people build the skills, mindsets, and behaviours needed to thrive in an AI-enabled future.

As the AI Learning Associate Director, you will serve as a strategic advisor and learning capability leader responsible for shaping, scaling and activating EY Canada's AI learning strategy, driving enterprise-wide AI skill development, and enabling our people to adopt AI in ways that create measurable business impact.

Reporting to the L&D Business Partner and working in close partnership with EY Canada's Chief Technology Officer and the Office of the CTO, you will help shape and execute enterprise-wide learning strategies that drive AI adoption, support workforce transformation, and build future-ready capabilities across the organization.

This highly visible role requires a blend of learning expertise, business acumen, stakeholder management, and change leadership. You will work across service lines, talent, technology, and leadership teams to identify emerging capability needs, design scalable solutions, and translate complex AI concepts into meaningful learning experiences that drive measurable business outcomes. Success in this role requires an agile, builder's mindset and the ability to thrive in a rapidly evolving environment where priorities, technologies, and workforce needs continue to shift. The successful candidate will be comfortable navigating ambiguity, rapidly translating emerging opportunities into action, and continuously adapting learning strategies to keep pace with change.

This job posting relates to an existing vacancy within our organization.

Your Key Responsibilities

Partner with senior business, L&D, and technology leaders to define capability priorities that support EY Canada's AI transformation strategy.
Develop and execute a comprehensive AI learning roadmap aligned to evolving business priorities and emerging technology trends.
Identify opportunities to accelerate AI adoption through innovative learning experiences, performance support tools, and capability-building initiatives.
Lead the firmwide design, development, and deployment of enterprise AI learning programs, learning paths, campaigns, and experiences.
Translate emerging AI priorities into scalable learning solutions that drive behaviour change and business impact.
Curate and integrate learning resources, programs, platforms, certifications, and thought leadership content to support a continuous learning culture.
Oversee the end-to-end lifecycle of strategic AI learning initiatives, ensuring delivery excellence and strong learning outcomes.
Collaborate with subject matter experts, external vendors, and subject matter experts across the business to lead the development of high-quality, business-relevant content and experiences.
Influence senior stakeholders and navigate competing priorities to achieve program objectives and organizational goals.
Monitor adoption trends, learner engagement, and business feedback to continuously evolve capability-building strategies.
Manage select program budgets, vendor relationships, and governance activities to ensure operational excellence.
Partner with Brand Marketing Communications and leadership teams to develop effective engagement, activation, and reinforcement plans.

A successful candidate for the AI Learning Associate Director role at EY Canada will possess a unique blend of skills, experience, and attributes that enable them to thrive in a fast-paced, transformative environment. Here’s what we’re looking for:

Skills And Attributes For Success

Strategic thinker with the ability to translate business priorities into innovative learning solutions.
Strong understanding of emerging AI trends, technologies, and use cases, with the ability to assess implications for workforce capability development and organizational transformation.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in fast-changing environments, bringing an entrepreneurial, agency-oriented mindset that embraces experimentation, rapid iteration, continuous learning, and adaptation as technologies and business priorities evolve.
Strong consulting and influencing skills, including experience working with executive stakeholders.
Deep understanding of adult learning principles, capability development, and organizational change.
Strong business acumen and curiosity regarding the impact of AI on workforce transformation and future skills.
Experience using data to guide decision-making and measure program effectiveness.
Exceptional project leadership, prioritization, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to navigate ambiguity and drive progress through collaboration and influence.

To qualify for the role, you must have

8+ years of experience in learning and development, talent development, workforce transformation, change management, or related fields.
Experience working with an LMS (preferably SuccessFactors) a plus.
Proficient in advanced capabilities in Excel (use of pivot tables and v-lookup) and PowerPoint.
Proficient in Zoom, MS Teams, Office 360 and SharePoint.
Demonstrated proficiency using AI and AI-powered productivity tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot and similar solutions) to enhance personal effectiveness, accelerate content creation, synthesize information, support decision-making, and improve business outcomes.
Experience applying AI to solve business problems, improve ways of working, or drive capability-building and adoption initiatives within an organization.
Bilingualism in English and French is an asset.

What We Offer

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. Plus, we offer:

Support and coaching from some of the most engaging colleagues in the industry
Learning opportunities to develop new skills and progress your career
The freedom and flexibility to handle your role in a way that’s right for you

EY reports salary ranges in accordance with applicable provincial pay transparency legislation. Individual salaries within the anticipated salary ranges noted below are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to internal equity, education, relevant experience, knowledge, and applicable skill sets.

Vancouver/Victoria: $126,800 to $211,300
Dieppe: $114,000 to $190,000

Inclusiveness at EY

Inclusiveness is at the heart of who we are and how we work. We’re committed to fostering an environment where differences are valued, policies and practices are equitable, and our people feel a sense of belonging. We embrace diversity and are committed to combating systemic racism, advancing gender equity and women in leadership, advocating for the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, promoting our neuroinclusion and accessibility initiatives, and are dedicated to amplifying the voices of Indigenous peoples (First Nations, Inuit, and Métis) nationally as we strive towards reconciliation. Our diverse experiences, abilities, backgrounds, and perspectives make our people unique and help guide us. Because when people feel free to be their authentic selves at work, they bring their best and are empowered to build a better working world.

Learn about our commitment to Inclusiveness at https://www.ey.com/en_ca/about-us/corporate-responsibility/equity

EY | Building a better working world

EY is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

EY teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. Fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, EY teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories.

At EY, we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools as one element of our recruitment process to enhance efficiency and improve the candidate experience. While AI supports us in our process, human judgment and decision-making remain integral in our candidate experience. We are committed to the responsible use of AI, and our practices are continuously reviewed and refined to ensure they align with ethical principles and regulatory requirements.

jobs.title: AVP, AI & Innovation
jobs.description:
Work Location:

Toronto, Ontario, Canada

Hours

37.5

Line Of Business

TD Securities

Pay Details

$155,000 - $215,000 CAD

TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.

As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.

Job Description

Role mandate

Lead the Applied AI and Innovation capability for TD Securities and build a high-performing team of applied AI specialists. Identify advances in AI that matter to the business and translate them into practical capabilities that can be tested, proven, and deployed in capital markets workflows.

This is a business-led senior technical leadership role requiring deep AI expertise, strong product judgment, and a pragmatic delivery mindset. The role connects emerging models, methods, and research with complex business problems and works across business, quantitative, data, engineering, and control teams to deliver measurable value.

Strategy and technical direction

Set the applied AI strategy, technical direction, and priorities across generative AI, agentic systems, decision intelligence, multimodal models, retrieval, reasoning, and human-agent operating models for TD Securities.
Assess research and industry developments in generative AI, agentic AI, machine learning, retrieval, reasoning, multimodal models, and related technologies, for practical relevance, then translate the most promising capabilities into experiments, product strategies, operating models, and value opportunities.
Determine where advanced AI provides a material advantage over conventional analytics, rules, or automation, avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Applied AI delivery and value creation

Identify and prioritize high-value opportunities; develop business cases, value hypotheses, adoption plans, measurable baselines, and value-realization frameworks.
Lead applied scientists in designing, building, testing, and improving AI solutions for complex, knowledge-intensive and analytical workflows.
Establish standards for experimentation, benchmarking, statistical rigor, error analysis, robustness, documentation, reproducibility, and production readiness.
Develop or adapt models and methods when existing solutions do not meet requirements for performance, latency, privacy, explainability, control, or cost.
Drive rapid prototyping while ensuring successful solutions can be engineered, governed, scaled, monitored, and supported in production.

Technical leadership

Provide senior technical oversight across model selection and adaptation, fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, agent orchestration, knowledge and semantic methods, tool use, planning, memory, context management, hybrid retrieval, reranking, evaluation, and inference optimization.
Design robust agentic and retrieval systems, spanning tool use, planning, memory, context management, hybrid retrieval and reranking, while proactively addressing scaling, data quality, evaluation blind spots and inference cost.
Set rigorous experimentation and evaluation standards, including controlled ablations, multi-seed testing, statistical significance, red teaming and contamination controls to ensure solutions are reliable and production-ready.
Anticipate and mitigate scaling bottlenecks, evaluation blind spots, data quality issues, model risk, security concerns, and inference cost.
Challenge architecture and model choices; lead design reviews and resolve significant trade-offs with Engineering, Data, Architecture, Technology, and control partners.

AI products and capability development

Apply product-management disciplines to AI capabilities, including vision, roadmaps, lifecycle management, prioritization, adoption, and value tracking.
Work directly with quantitative practitioners, traders, bankers, risk specialists, data scientists, and engineers to frame problems and design practical AI solutions.
Establish reusable AI components, evaluation frameworks, implementation patterns, and technical standards that accelerate delivery across teams.
Apply AI to information extraction and synthesis, decision support, workflow automation, quantitative and analytical tasks, client intelligence, risk analysis, and other complex processes.
Partner with engineering and delivery teams to move validated prototypes into reliable production capabilities.

People and capability leadership

Build, lead, and develop a multidisciplinary applied AI team with a high bar for technical quality, scientific rigor, engineering discipline, and measurable impact.
Lead through technical credibility by authoring design documents, running architecture and technical reviews, and setting expectations for code, experiments, and system quality.

Governance, risk, and responsible adoption

Partner with Risk, Compliance, Legal, Information Security, Technology, and enterprise AI governance teams to ensure responsible, controlled, auditable, and explainable adoption.
Define guardrails, escalation paths, adoption controls, measurement routines, and governance artifacts for AI products and agentic workflows, while preserving clear human accountability for material decisions.

Decision authorities

Prioritize the AI product and transformation portfolio with front-office sponsors and enabling partners.
Determine which emerging capabilities warrant experimentation and which prototypes have sufficient evidence to progress toward production.
Recommend investments in models, tooling, platforms, compute, talent, and external partnerships.
Escalate material risk, control, data, compliance, or technology dependencies to the appropriate accountable partners.

The Role Shares Responsibilities And Decision Interfaces With

Front Office leaders for opportunity prioritization, workflow design, commercial impact, adoption, and value realization.
Data Product teams for reusable, business-ready data; semantic context; quality; lineage; provenance; metadata; and AI-ready information structures.
Technology and Architecture for secure implementation, integration, platform alignment, resiliency, production readiness, and sustainable support.
Risk, Compliance, Legal, Information Security, and enterprise AI Governance for control design, policy alignment, approvals, responsible AI, and auditability.
Finance and Business Management for business cases, budgets, benefits tracking, operating leverage, and value realization.
Operations, Change Management, Human Resources, and Learning for workflow change, adoption, training, role impacts, and capability building.
Product and Delivery partners for execution planning, backlog prioritization, stakeholder engagement, success metrics, and delivery discipline.
Approved universities, research institutes, vendors, and open-source communities for collaboration, talent pipelines, and knowledge exchange.
Key measures will balance technical quality, adoption, and realized business impact:
Realized value from AI-enabled products, capabilities, and workflow transformation, including productivity, decision quality, revenue support, risk insight, or control effectiveness.
Delivery of approved roadmap milestones, business cases, benefits plans, and strategic transformation objectives.
Adoption, outcome improvement, reliability, and production performance of deployed AI capabilities.
Number, maturity, and reuse of AI components, evaluation frameworks, implementation patterns, workflows, and skills.
Team growth, talent development, stakeholder confidence, and cross-functional delivery effectiveness.
Portfolio, project, cost-centre, and value-realization targets to be confirmed.
This role is generally not directly client-facing. It creates client and shareholder value by improving how front-office teams serve clients, identify opportunities, make decisions, manage risk, and execute work.
Improves the speed, quality, and consistency of client coverage through AI-enabled insights, workflow tools, and decision support.
Reduces manual effort and accelerates access to relevant business context and information.
Supports revenue generation and relationship management by helping teams prepare more effectively and act on insights faster.
Simplifies fragmented workflows and embeds intelligence into day-to-day processes.
Strengthens control, transparency, and consistency through governed, explainable, reusable AI capabilities.

Education

PhD strongly preferred in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Statistics, Mathematics, Operations Research, Engineering, Physics, or a related quantitative discipline. A research-intensive master’s degree may be considered with an exceptional record of applied technical leadership.

Experience And Technical Capabilities

Typically 8+ years of progressive experience in applied AI, machine learning, data science, quantitative research, or advanced analytics, including leadership of multidisciplinary technical teams.
Demonstrated success translating research into robust, production-used systems in complex, regulated, or high-consequence environments.
Deep expertise in several areas such as large language models, natural language processing, retrieval and reasoning, agentic systems, multimodal learning, graph methods, time-series modelling, causal inference, optimization, reinforcement learning, or probabilistic modelling.
Expert command of experimental design, statistical inference, benchmarking, ablation studies, error analysis, model evaluation, reproducibility, contamination controls, and scientific peer review.
Strong hands-on fluency in Python and modern AI/ML ecosystems, with the ability to review code, experiments, model behaviour, architecture, and data pipelines.
Strong understanding of production AI architecture, including feature and data pipelines, vector and graph retrieval, model serving, APIs, distributed compute, cloud platforms, MLOps and LLMOps, observability, security, latency, resiliency, and cost optimization.
Technical depth to challenge designs, assess feasibility and risk, resolve architecture trade-offs, and partner credibly with data, engineering, quantitative, and technology teams.
Experience building and developing applied science or research teams, including talent assessment, mentoring, organizational design, and capability building.
Ability to engage credibly with quantitative practitioners, engineers, data scientists, risk specialists, traders, bankers, and senior technology leaders.
Capital markets or financial-services experience strongly preferred; experience with market, client, transaction, research, risk, or unstructured financial data is advantageous.
Executive communication skills to explain technical findings, uncertainty, limitations, and investment choices precisely without oversimplification.

Who We Are

TD Securities offers a wide range of capital markets products and services to corporate, government, and institutional clients who choose us for our innovation, execution, and experience. With more than 6,500 professionals operating out of 40 cities across the globe, we strive to make every interaction, product and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple. Our services include underwriting and distributing new issues, providing trusted advice and industry-leading insight, extending access to global markets, and delivering integrated transaction banking solutions. jobs.title: Vice President, Analytics & Health Outcomes
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. We believe health care is a right, not a privilege, and we are committed to improving health outcomes, advancing health equity, and building a future where every Canadian can reach their full health and well-being potential.
Through our unique integrated payer-provider ("payvider") model, we offer insurance, administer benefits, and pay claims as a ‘payer’ while offering health care services such as mental health, pharmacy, telemedicine, and chronic disease management as a ‘provider’. As a non-profit social enterprise without shareholders, we reinvest our excess earnings to directly support underserved communities. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All.
At GreenShield, our culture is where purpose meets passion and performance. Our teams work as one to deliver meaningful, measurable impact for the people and communities we serve.

THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL

Reporting to the SVP, Product, Experience & Health Outcomes, the Vice President, Analytics and Health Outcomes is a strategic senior leadership role responsible for turning GreenShield’s data into actionable insights, measurable outcomes, and clear narratives that inform priorities, support decision-making, and demonstrate impact. This leader will work across the organization to connect analytics and insights to enterprise priorities and measurable impact in a way that helps leaders understand what is happening, why it matters, and where to act.

This role will be responsible for:

Lead enterprise analytics and outcomes capabilities, ensuring data is used to inform priorities, guide investment decisions, and measure impact across the enterprise.
Translate complex data into clear insights, narratives, and recommendations that help executives, product teams, clinical leaders, clients, and partners understand where to act and how to create measurable value.
Build scalable measurement practices that help GreenShield assess performance, outcomes, and impact across its portfolio.
Develop clear, evidence-based insights for internal and external stakeholders to demonstrate impact.
Partner cross-functionally to embed analytics and outcome measures into planning, decision-making, client insights, and performance management.
Use data-driven insights to support better experiences, decisions, and outcomes.
Provide thought leadership on data quality, governance, privacy, responsible AI, and scalable analytics practices, working closely with Technology and enterprise data teams to ensure the right data foundations are in place.
Build and lead a high-performing team that combines analytical depth, business judgment, storytelling, and a practical orientation toward measurable outcomes.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

15+ years of progressive analytics experience in health care, benefits, insurance, consulting, or a related field, including senior leadership accountability for analytics, insight generation, and business impact.
Proven ability to turn data into insight, insight into action, and action into measurable business, customer, and health outcomes.
Exceptional storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex analysis into simple, credible, executive-ready narratives for internal leaders, clients, partners, and external audiences.
Business-oriented analytics leader who can ask the right questions, define the right measures, challenge assumptions, and connect data to decisions that improve performance and impact.
Experience building outcome frameworks, dashboards, scorecards, insights, analytics products, or executive reporting that drive decision-making.
Advanced analytics expertise, including predictive modelling, segmentation, measurement design, statistical analysis, data visualization, and practical application to business, customer, and health outcome questions.
Strong advanced analytics capability, including familiarity with AI and machine learning applications.
A collaborative, practical, and outcomes-focused leadership style, with the ability to operate at both strategic and execution levels in a fast-moving environment.

WHAT WE OFFER

Base Salary:
Range exempt
Offer positioning:
Determined using relevant experience, skills, internal equity and current market data.
Additional compensation:
Eligible for a discretionary target bonus.
Total rewards:
Health and dental coverage, retirement savings, paid time off and well-being support (up to $10,000 per year for mental health).
Posting disclosures:
This is for an existing vacancy.
Work model:
Hybrid

THE CULTURE

We believe a career should be meaningful. Not just a means to earn a living. Our culture is one where everyone's voice is heard and valued. Because that’s what it takes to create better health for all. We dare to challenge the status quo. And we’re driven by people who have challenged theirs. We believe that your workplace should empower you to be the best version of yourself. That’s why we provide a place where you can be inspired, challenged, and rewarded.

Where your growth means our growth.
Where your voice is heard and valued.
Where your work has purpose. And purpose matters.

We believe our people are critical to our overall success. Inclusivity makes us a stronger, smarter and more informed organization. Being intentionally inclusive of diverse backgrounds, perspectives and experiences will enhance our company culture to positively impact how we support our communities. A career at GreenShield isn’t just about personal achievements, it's about making a difference together.

Here’s to Better Health for All!

A FEW MORE DETAILS

Proficiency in English is required for this position. As part of this role, you will be required to communicate with colleagues or customers who use English as their primary language. By requiring English proficiency for this position, we aim to ensure that our employees can excel in their roles, collaborate, and communicate effectively, and contribute to the success of our organization.

jobs.title: Chief Courts Information Officer
jobs.description:
Job Description

On behalf of our public-sector client, Affinity is seeking a Chief Courts Information Officer to be accountable for the strategic leadership, governance, and delivery of information management (IM), information technology (IT), and digital services for the Courts. The CCIO ensures that court information systems, digital services, and technology investments support judicial independence, court administration, access to justice, operational efficiency, privacy, and security.

Responsibilities

Develop and implement information management strategies and polices to ensure the secure and efficient handling of Court information.
Project management, change management and strategic planning processes for the effective delivery and management of both short and long-term information technology goals set by the judiciary.
Represent the interests of the judiciary recognizing judicial independence in their day-today operations of and/or projects involving implementing and/or updating software, databases and digital tools used by the judiciary or involving judicial data and court information.
Must operate with full confidence of the Chief Justices and the Chief Judge, be discreet as required and understand the highly confidential and sensitive nature of the work that they perform.
The Chief Court Information Officer (“CCIO”) must have the ability to work cooperatively and harmoniously with all members of the judiciary and both senior and front-line court administration staff, as we as internal and external stakeholders.
Lead the modernization of court information systems, including case management, e-filing, digital evidence, and courtroom technology.

Qualifications

Education and/or training involving computer science, information technology, cyber security or related field.
Significant work experience, preferably 5 years or more, in information technology and information governance, with a focus on cybersecurity and records retention.
Strong understanding of legal and regulatory requirements related to information management, cybersecurity, and records retention.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective information management strategies for an increasingly digital legal work environment.
Extensive experience conducting IT and information security research and providing advice and opinions, preferably at a senior executive level.
Demonstrated ability to prepare written opinions, memoranda and reports.
The incumbent must have a superior understanding of the principles of judicial independence and possess strong political acumen and experience in the application of discretion and diplomacy to ensure positive outcomes and confidence in the administration of justice.
Well-developed planning and organizational skills in order to accomplish the position’s responsibilities and meet target dates and set priorities.
Experience using MS Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio and Outlook and online legal research databases which may be used by the judiciary. Familiarity with JUDICLOUD (federally appointed judges email network) and/or PowerBI is considered an asset.
Stakeholder engagement - Build effective relationships with the judiciary, court administrators, justice partners, central government IT organizations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the Courts on inter jurisdictional, justice sector, and government technology forums, as required.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
On-site attendance is a mandatory requirement for this role.
Must be able to provide a satisfactory criminal record check and security clearance.
The Resource will be required to execute a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) and maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all information obtained or accessed in the course of performing the Services.
Relevant certifications such as the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
A law degree from an accredited university or college recognized in Manitoba.

You can also earn up to $50,000 for helping us find new clients. We believe in creating long term relationships between clients and consultants that foster a mutually beneficial partnership. Affinity is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

For more information on Affinity, please visit www.affinity-group.ca
